blocks.text: Condo buildings in Connaught Heights
Streets, schools and getting around Connaught Heights

items.t: Connaught Heights is the City of New Westminster's west-end mainland neighbourhood, around 22nd Street Station, London Street and Marine Way; the City lists Connaught Heights among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, so the City name and the board (GVR) name match. Nearby areas: the West End and Moody Park to the east, Burnaby across the city's west boundary, and Queensborough across the Queensborough Bridge to the south-east.

Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere in Connaught Heights — the sub-area's entire listed stock in September 2026 was detached. New Westminster's condo stock concentrates in Downtown, Uptown and the Quay, east of this neighbourhood. The growth pressure here is prospective: the 22nd Street Station area is identified in the OCP as a Frequent Transit Development Area.

SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: New Westminster condos & townhomes median was $560,000 in September 2026 ($587/sqft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days on market) and the detached median was $1,365,000. There is no Connaught Heights condo median — the segment did not exist locally that month.

Transit anchors: 22nd Street Station (Expo Line) is at the area; TransLink routes from the station include the 100 (Marpole), 101 (Lougheed Station), 104 (Annacis Island) and 128 (Braid Station). Main roads: Marine Way / Stewardson Way and 20th Street / 22nd Street, linking west to Burnaby and south across the Queensborough Bridge via Highway 91A.

Neighbourhood anchors: Connaught Heights Elementary at 2201 London Street, Connaught Heights Park (shared with the school), and Grimston Park, the community park at the west end of the city. The area has minimal retail services per the City's small-sites consultation record.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Connaught Heights

items.t: Transit-Oriented Development Areas: provincial Transit Oriented Development Areas introduced in 2024 enable density within 800 metres of the City's five SkyTrain stations, including 22nd Street, and the City is amending the OCP to implement TOD Area extensions — a February 17, 2026 City report addresses extending the "Residential – Limited Mid Rise" designation to properties on the outer edges of the provincial TOD areas. This is the mechanism that will eventually create condo stock here; today it changes land value, not the building list.

blocks.text: Good to know about Connaught Heights

items.t: The station got new elevators before the neighbourhood got a vision.

Council endorsed a new identity for the station area in December 2024. The reGENERATE Vision process ran 2023–2024 and the final Vision was endorsed by Council in December 2024, built on eight "Big Moves" — any Connaught Heights purchase near the station is a purchase inside an endorsed redesign area, even though no condo exists there yet.

One of the City's two small-sites lots is park-locked. The consultation record for the City's affordable-housing small-sites initiative notes a Crown Land Grant on 2038 Ninth Avenue identifying the property for parks and recreation purposes — a buyer assuming both London Street / Ninth Avenue lots are future housing sites is only half right, and the City has also heard that Connaught Heights needs more parkland.

The elementary school park is not always public. Connaught Heights Park is shared with Connaught Heights Elementary, and the City's small-sites consultation heard the shared park is not always accessible to the community during the school day; a recommended action in the City's Comprehensive Parks Plan is to acquire more parkland in Connaught Heights.
September 2026 was a zero month for the whole sub-area.

The city's density is someone else's neighbourhood. The 2021 Census counted 78,916 people in New Westminster at 5,052 people per sq. km — among the densest cities in Canada — yet this west-end pocket remains RS-zoned detached houses beside an Expo Line station, which is precisely why the province's TOD rules and the City's vision both target it.

items.t: Connaught Heights is New Westminster's west-end mainland neighbourhood, around 22nd Street Station, London Street and Marine Way; the City lists Connaught Heights among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, so the City name and the GVR board name match.

Nearby areas: the West End and Moody Park to the east, Burnaby across the city's west boundary, and Queensborough across the Queensborough Bridge to the south-east. Note for board geography: north-arm is a New Westminster board sub-area — it is a different sub-area from Connaught Heights and nothing from it is filed here.
The planning pressure point is the 22nd Street Station area, which the OCP identifies as a Frequent Transit Development Area.

New Westminster community medians for September 2026 were detached $1,365,000 and "Condos & Townhomes" combined $560,000 ($587/sqft, 95% sale-to-list, 27 days on market). (SnapStats covers New Westminster as a community; there is no Connaught Heights townhome figure to cite.)

Transit: 22nd Street Station (Expo Line) is in the area; TransLink routes from the station include the 100 (Marpole), 101 (Lougheed Station), 104 (Annacis Island) and 128 (Braid Station). Roads: Marine Way / Stewardson Way and 20th Street / 22nd Street, linking west to Burnaby and south across the Queensborough Bridge via Highway 91A.
Schools: SD40 catchments are address-based. School names use Ministry-listed names only.
Library and care: New Westminster Public Library Main Branch, 716 6th Avenue (Uptown); Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, Sapperton (Fraser Health), is the city's hospital.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Connaught Heights

items.t: Depreciation reports / CRF (provincial strata frame, stated for cross-shopping buyers): since July 1, 2024, strata corporations with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years, not deferrable by vote; since Nov 1, 2023, at least 10% of the annual operating budget must go to the contingency reserve fund.

Rental-restriction bylaws are void (strata): since Nov 24, 2022, no BC strata residential rental-restriction bylaw is valid; short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw. For a Connaught Heights house, suite rental is a municipal question (see zoning below), not a strata question.
Fee-simple position (the form that actually exists here): a Connaught Heights house is fee-simple — no strata, no Form B, no strata fees.

City zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 governs. Houses sit in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s. 310). RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5; the RS districts allow secondary suites, and laneway / carriage houses are regulated under the same bylaw. The bylaw's s. 410 "(RT-2) Townhouse Districts" schedule states the district's intent is to allow townhouse development and permits row houses or townhouses.

blocks.text: Good to know about Connaught Heights

items.t: One of the City's two small-sites lots is park-locked: the City's affordable-housing consultation for 2035 London Street and 2038 Ninth Avenue recorded a Crown Land Grant on 2038 Ninth Avenue identifying the property for parks and recreation purposes — a fact that affects what can actually be built beside those lots, whatever the project renderings suggest.

The elementary school park is not always public: Connaught Heights Park is shared with Connaught Heights Elementary, and the City's consultation heard the shared park is not always accessible to the community during the school day; a recommended action in the City's Comprehensive Parks Plan is to acquire more parkland in Connaught Heights. Grimston Park is the community park at the west end.

Minimal retail is a planning fact, not an impression: the City's small-sites consultation recorded that the area has minimal retail services. The station, not a high street, is the neighbourhood's amenity anchor.

The city runs its own electrical utility (dated context): New Westminster operates its own electrical utility alongside City water/sewer services — a utility-bill difference from every neighbouring municipality that a relocating buyer will not see in a listing.

Density bragging rights belong to other neighbourhoods: the 2021 Census counted 78,916 people in New Westminster at 5,052 people per sq. km — but the density is Downtown, the Quay and Uptown's, not Connaught Heights', whose listed stock that census-era planning still describes is detached houses beside an Expo Line station.

items.t: Established-street house lots: single-detached houses under the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s.310) of Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, with secondary suites allowed and laneway / carriage houses regulated under the same bylaw — the sub-area's actual ground-oriented form. No condo building or townhome complex name in Connaught Heights was confirmed on a developer or strata source.

Lot character from the zone: RS-1 sets a minimum site area of 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) and a floor space ratio of 0.5. That is the zone minimum, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel.

Serviced position, as the City states it: New Westminster operates its own electrical utility and City water / sewer services, and the City's subdivision guide states new lots must be adequately serviced with water, sewers, underground electrical, communications, street lighting, roads, sidewalks and street trees. Servicing for any single vacant or assembly parcel is confirmed through that subdivision process.
No ALR percentage split is stated.

Flood position: the City's floodplain study zones only the city's low-lying edges — Zone 1 Queensborough, Zone 2 west-end Fraser River industrial land, Zone 3 the Quay waterfront and Zone 4 the Brunette River industrial area. No floodplain zone for Connaught Heights' residential streets was confirmed.

Market context, labelled correctly: New Westminster is a SnapStats-covered community. SnapStats has no land category, and no detached figure below is a land figure. blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Connaught Heights

items.t: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 governs. Houses sit in the Single Detached Residential Districts (RS series, s.310) — RS-1: minimum site area 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR 0.5; the RS districts allow secondary suites and regulate laneway / carriage houses.

Plan: "Our City 2041," the Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 7925, 2017, governs the area, and the 22nd Street Station area is identified in it as a Frequent Transit Development Area — one of the areas where the City directs higher-density, transit-supportive growth. Confirm the exact OCP designation for a station-adjacent lot with the City before pricing in redevelopment value.

SSMUH / added units: in the RS districts, secondary suites are allowed and laneway / carriage houses are regulated under Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001, within the RS-1 minimum site area (557.40 m²) and 0.5 FSR.

Subdivision + servicing requirements — confirmed bylaw, process stated: subdivision is regulated by the Subdivision and Development Control Bylaw No. 7142, 2007, which requires all subdivisions be approved by the City's Approving Officer (the Director of Engineering Services) and ensures new lots are adequately serviced and meet the Zoning Bylaw's minimum lot size and frontage requirements. The City's process runs pre-application, application, and — where required — a Works & Services Agreement with detailed servicing drawings by an engineering consultant, before final approval and Land Title registration. Parcel-level standards are confirmed through that process; none is quoted lot-by-lot here.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Connaught Heights ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

New Westminster property taxes and utilities: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on current taxes remaining unpaid on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on any unpaid balance on September 3, 2026. The City operates its own electrical utility alongside City water / sewer services.

faq.a: The neighbourhood's attached living is secondary suites and laneway/carriage houses inside houses — not strata product.
faq.q: Are there really no condos in Connaught Heights?

faq.a: The city's condo stock is in Downtown, Uptown and the Quay, east of the neighbourhood — the New Westminster community condos & townhomes median was $560,000 in September 2026 (SnapStats, community level).
faq.q: Where do Connaught Heights downsizers buy condos instead?

faq.a: The City's 22nd Street Station Area Bold Vision (the reGENERATE Vision) was endorsed by Council in December 2024 after a vision process launched in spring 2023; the City describes the station area as a key growth area in the OCP, planned to become a high-density mixed-use core centred on the transit hub. It is a vision and planning framework — it has not yet produced a condo building in the sub-area.
faq.q: What is the reGENERATE / Bold Vision plan for 22nd Street Station?

faq.a: Provincial TOD Areas enable density within 800 metres of SkyTrain stations, 22nd Street included, and the City is amending the OCP to implement TOD extensions (February 17, 2026 report). Marine Way listings already market assembled lots on that basis (one cites a minimum 20-storey tower at 5.0 FSR). What a specific lot may build is a City confirmation, not a listing claim — verify the designation and zoning before pricing in redevelopment value.
faq.q: What does Bill 47 / the TOD Area mean for a house near the station?

faq.a: Yes — the Zoning Bylaw's RS districts allow secondary suites and regulate laneway/carriage houses; RS-1 sets a 557.40 m² (6,000 sq. ft.) minimum site area and a 0.5 floor space ratio. Those units are rental/family space inside a house purchase, not strata condos, and they do not come with a Form B or a strata.
faq.q: Can a Connaught Heights house add a suite or laneway house?

faq.a: Individual townhouse-form houses exist; a complex does not, on the record.
faq.q: Are there really no townhouses in Connaught Heights?

faq.a: No — the stock is fee-simple houses: no strata, no Form B, no strata fees. Diligence is title, Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001 and registered covenants.
faq.q: Is a Connaught Heights house a strata purchase?

faq.a: RT-A (s.405) and RT-B (s.406) are the newer townhouse districts in Zoning Bylaw No. 6680. A site needs at least 836.1 m² (9,000 sq. ft.) of site area, at least 20 m of frontage and lane access. The older townhouse districts are RT-2 to RT-2C, and RT-3, RT-3A and RT-3B in Queensborough.
